items.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
items.snippet: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. Here's why it mattered.

items.title: AI has solved a host of big math problems—here's why this threatens the whole field of mathematics
items.snippet: For many, the year 2026 will be remembered as the one when mathematics had an identity crisis and forever changed. Frontier (cutting-edge) AI models made by OpenAI and Anthropic made stunning progress on hundreds of open problems that have baffled mathematicians for decades—and centuries in some cases.

items.snippet: There is a widespread notion among violinists: A violin "opens up" as it is played, which is to say its sound gradually improves. items.title: Genetic mosaic helps explain diverse forms of Darwin's finches
items.snippet: Darwin's finches are known for their varied beaks, which help them take advantage of different food sources in the Galápagos Islands. Much previous research has focused on seed-eating ground finches, but their relatives that search for insects in forested areas have received less attention.

items.title: Recipe for one of the world's most important cancer drugs uncovered: Tobacco plants could produce the medicine
items.snippet: More people around the world will receive a cancer diagnosis at some point in their lives. As this trend is expected to continue, researchers have been working to crack the code of how the widely used cancer drug Taxol (paclitaxel) is naturally produced, with the aim of making its production cheaper and more efficient in the future.

items.title: Electron microscopy reveals the headquarters of poxviruses
items.snippet: Mpox remains a smoldering threat, with recent clusters in Brazil, Thailand and Austria and ongoing hot spots across multiple African countries. Other poxviruses also endanger human or animal health. items.title: Consumers, oblivious of being targeted, find online ads helpful
items.snippet: Most online shoppers know that ads strategically follow them across sites, a mechanism known as "ad retargeting." A new study led by Penn State researchers found that consumers find these targeted ads helpful, but explaining why they are seeing an ad can backfire by increasing concerns about being watched.

items.title: NASA spacecraft data reveal how solar system's tail shifts over 14 years
items.snippet: A Southwest Research Institute-led study is the first to map out the distinct motion paths of the heliotail lobes across a 14-year period using data from NASA's Interstellar Boundary Explorer (IBEX) spacecraft. By identifying the paths followed by these lobes, the study provides a better understanding of how solar activity shapes the heliotail.

items.snippet: Medical imaging technologies have transformed how scientists and physicians visualize blood flowing through the human heart, but even the most advanced imaging techniques cannot capture every detail of fluid motion. items.title: Satellite observations show how rain breaks up Earth's natural sunshades
items.snippet: Delivering on its promise, the European Space Agency's EarthCARE satellite is already yielding new insights into the role that clouds play in regulating Earth's climate. The latest findings shed light on one of the processes that leads to the breakup of vast, bright cloud formations that help keep our planet cool—with rain emerging as a key driver.
